sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know from B1 Unit 38 that an order or a request is reported with *que* and the imperfect subjunctive after a past verb: *Me dijo que viniera*, *Me pidió que le ayudara*. (You know the imperfect subjunctive forms from B1 Unit 4.) This lesson adds two points.

sections.title: Order or request → reported
rows: Me dijo que cerrara la ventana.
Me pidió que cerrara la ventana.
Nos pidió que no cerráramos la puerta.

sections.title: New 1: a question can be a request
sections.content: A request is often asked as a question: *¿Puedes…?*, *¿Podrías…?*. When the person wants you to do something, you report it as a request with *pidió que* and the subjunctive. Reporting it with *preguntó si* would report a real question about whether you are able: *Me preguntó si podía cerrar la ventana* (she wanted to know whether I could).

sections.title: New 2: the reporting verb sets the tense
sections.content: The subjunctive follows the reporting verb. After a past verb (*pidió*, *dijo*) use the imperfect subjunctive: *Ana me pidió que te llamara*. After the present perfect or the present (*ha pedido*, *me pide*) use the present subjunctive, the one you know from A2 Unit 27: *Ana me ha pedido que te llame*.

items.spanish: Luis me pidió que cerrara la ventana.
items.english: Luis asked me to close the window.

items.spanish: Ana me ha pedido que te llame esta tarde.
items.english: Ana has asked me to call you this afternoon.

items.spanish: El médico me dijo que descansara unos días.
items.english: The doctor told me to rest for a few days.

items.spanish: Nos pidieron que no habláramos en voz alta.
items.english: They asked us not to talk loudly.

sections.content: Remember the difference you know from B1 Unit 38: *Dijo que venía* reports information (indicative), *Dijo que viniera* reports an order (subjunctive).
